extracted.intended_audience: literate general readers in Britain and America interested in American life, theater, literature, and public figures
extracted.subtask_description: Autobiographical essays and reminiscences (Whitman) giving vivid accounts of 19th-century American theaters, actors, travel, politics, and Abraham Lincoln, with evaluative commentary about art, literature, and public character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement and ovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bowery audiences produced 'long-kept-up tempests of hand-clapping'—not delicate applause but 'electric force and muscle' from thousands of listeners, seen as an integral part of the theatrical experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure a performance's immediate popular success by the intensity, duration, and physicality of audience response (sustained clapping, collective emotional reaction), especially in working-class or populist venues where raw energy matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to create and hold a hush/suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: An actor 'who could make more of the said hush or wait, and hold the audience in an indescribable, half-delicious, half-irritating suspense' (Whitman's description of Booth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how effectively the performer controls silence and anticipatory stillness—entrances, measured pauses, and restrained gestures that produce concentrated audience attention and suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnetism and individual idiosyncrasy
rubrics_metrics.description: Art-utterance's decisive factor is 'the subtle and powerful something special to the individual'—a personal magnetism or idiosyncrasy that conquers the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a performer's unique personal stamp that vitalizes material beyond technical skill; originality of manner, charisma, and personal color are decisive in artistic success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitalizing tradition with individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Booth was 'royal heir and legitimate representative of the Garrick-Kemble-Siddons dramatic traditions; but he vitalized ... with his own electric personal idiosyncrasy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess balance between reverence for classical/traditional technique and the artist's capacity to infuse those traditions with fresh, personal life—neither mindless imitation nor mere novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive energy, abandon, and emotional fire
rubrics_metrics.description: Words like 'fire, energy, abandon' found in Booth gave them 'unprecedented meanings'; the power to deliver 'a sting to hauteur or the taunt.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate the performer's energetic commitment and ability to convey raw emotion convincingly—intensity, clarity of emotional focus, and control of dramatic force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocalization: clarity without musicality
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'charm of unswervingly perfect vocalization without trenching at all on mere melody, the province of music.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate vocal precision, diction, and expressive shaping that communicates power and nuance without becoming sing-songy; voice should serve meaning and emotion first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to produce physical/emotional reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: A performance (e.g., the 'dream scene') that caused 'a shudder through every nervous system in the audience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the piece elicits visceral audience responses (shudder, sob, laugh)—evidence of deep emotional impact beyond intellectual appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditorium as part of the show (sociological context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman treats 'the whole crowded auditorium, and what seeth'd in it, and flush'd from its faces and eyes' as part of the performance experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating performances or theatrical culture, include the composition and behavior of the audience (class, decorum, expectations) and how performer and program serve or exploit that social milieu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gossipy, informal, veracious prose style for memoir
rubrics_metrics.description: Preface instruction: 'take the following pages, as you do some long and gossippy letter ... lazily and informally, but ever veraciously.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this kind of book, aim for conversational, off-hand, intimate letter-like prose that privileges truthful recollection and personal tone over formal literary artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of American private life and common people
rubrics_metrics.description: The volume aims to present 'a common individual New World private life ... portraying American life-sights and incidents as they actually occurred' and to promote 'GOOD-WILL BETWEEN THE COMMON PEOPLE OF ALL NATIONS.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value authenticity, representative incidents, local color, and sympathetic depiction of everyday people; the writer should foreground common-sense experiences and democratic sympathies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature's democratic mission and civic function
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature—'a new, superb, democratic literature'—is 'to be the medicine and lever' and a chief influence in modern civilization; equal force should uphold political claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge literary work partly on its democratic reach and civic usefulness: does it broaden access, represent the masses, and contribute morally/intellectually to society, not merely entertain elites?

rubrics_metrics.name: Blending ideal with practical (as a mark of greatness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dowden's comment invoked: Shakespeare blends ideal and practical; Whitman analogizes Lincoln as doing in life what Shakespeare did in poetic expression—blending ideal with the practical or realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing public figures or works, value the ability to unite lofty ideals with pragmatic action; moral vision combined with concrete effectiveness is a criterion of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes of Lincoln's greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman's evaluative checklist: Lincoln had 'indomitable firmness (even obstinacy) on rare occasions' for great points; was 'easy, flexible, tolerant' on minor matters; had mystical, abstract, moral and spiritual foundations; a passion for the Union; a deep religious nature; Western, non‑conventional originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a leader's greatness by a constellation of traits: sustained moral/spiritual core, decisive firmness on vital issues, flexibility on lesser ones, profound religious or ethical grounding, passionate commitment to central causes (here, the Union), and originality rooted in life experience rather than mere convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel/journalistic vividness and local color
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman's travel notes emphasize concrete sensory details—coffee from a Creole woman, 'cobblers' with strawberries, levee scenes, steamboat difficulties—and chance encounters with captains and boatmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For travel or journalistic pieces, prioritize sensory detail, memorable incidental characters, and small domestic scenes that give larger cultural insight; personal anecdote and precise observation strengthen veracity and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of social context to political/legal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on the Attorney General's office and pardons: social/economic condition (property > $20,000) affects legal process; pardons conditioned on respecting abolition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reporting or evaluating postwar reconstruction/legal measures, include how social/economic thresholds and political pressures shape administrative outcomes and moral/constitutional conditions.
